---
title: "Connect an AI agent"
subtitle: "The Flux AI Bundle, its status, and your own skills"
---

Flux includes the tools, skills and context that let agents work with your project.
Click **AI** in the title bar, or use **Ctrl+K** → **AI status**, to open the monitor.
**Pin** moves the same panel into its own window; **Dock** brings it back.

## Connect Claude Code or Codex

Click **Connect** on the agent's card. Flux installs its skill, registers its MCP
server and installs supported refresh hooks. A replacement shows the exact before
and after text for your confirmation. Flux preserves unrelated settings and keeps
backups. Restart open agent sessions afterward. In Codex, review and trust new
hooks in **/hooks**.

Copy the command on the card into your agent: `/flux-connect <project path>` for
Claude Code, or `$flux-connect <project path>` for Codex. With no project open,
the command uses `global` to introduce Flux and your user context.
**Other agents…** gives manual MCP instructions.

**Repair** checks and repairs the same integration. **Disconnect** removes only
Flux-owned integration and restores prior registrations where safe; edited skills
are kept. Your projects stay available. Connecting or repairing another app's
configuration always starts with your click.

## Read the status

The titlebar dot is green when the bundle is ready for a connected agent, amber
when it needs attention, and red when a connected integration or shared part is
broken. Detected agents that are not connected need attention. Dismissing the
one-time **Connect an AI agent** Home card remembers that choice; it never hides
an actual error.

The panel has four sections:

- **Agents** shows installed versions and each agent's skill, registration,
  responding MCP, published user skills and refresh hook.
- **Bundle** shows the launcher and its owning install, the manual, user context,
  rendering and your Skills.
- **Sessions** shows the agents connected to this project, their watching and live
  badges, queues, current claims and connection times. **Stop watching** releases
  the session's claims and tells its wait loop to stop.
- **This project** shows this window's live bridge, saved inbox counts and last
  connection. Save edits to margin comments to include them in these counts.

Expand a row for its paths, version, last check, error and available fix.
**Run doctor** performs fresh execution checks, including the MCP handshake and a
small figure render, with results as each check finishes. **Copy diagnostics** runs
those checks and copies the doctor JSON. Vendor configuration values are kept out
of status and diagnostics; they appear only in a replacement you are confirming.

The panel paints its cached status immediately. Cheap probes refresh it on open,
after setup and every ten minutes. Full doctor checks run only when requested.
Execution checks say **Not checked** until a doctor result is available.

## Your skills

In **Bundle → Skills**, click **New skill…**, or use **Ctrl+K** → **New agent skill…**.
Enter a short lowercase name with hyphens, such as `stats-conventions`. Flux creates
a folder with a starter `SKILL.md` and opens it in your default editor, just like
**Open global rules**. Describe when to use the procedure, its steps and checks.

**Reveal in folder** opens the skills location. Skills are published to connected
agents and kept in sync: invoke `/stats-conventions` in Claude Code or
`$stats-conventions` in Codex. **Re-publish** checks publication now. Name collisions
and edited vendor copies are reported and preserved.

## What is the AI bundle?

| Part | What it gives agents | Where it lives | How it gets there |
|---|---|---|---|
| Launcher + `flux` CLI | every verb from any shell | `<binDir>/flux` (+ `flux-connect`) → the app's bundled CLI | written by Flux on every start (§6.1) |
| Flux MCP server | typed tools, images, live tools, inbox, watch | `"<launcher>" mcp` | registered with an agent by **Connect** (§9.1) |
| `flux-connect` skill | the one command | `~/.claude/skills/flux-connect`, `~/.agents/skills/flux-connect` | **Connect** |
| Your skills | `/stats-conventions` anywhere | `UserContext/Skills` → published to each connected agent | **Connect**, then kept in sync (§8.12a) |
| Flux manual (FluxContext) | how to use Flux | `<FluxConfig>/Context/FluxContext` | synced by Flux on start |
| Your context (UserContext) | who you are, your rules | `<FluxConfig>/Context/UserContext` | yours (seeded blank) |
| Figure rendering | agents can *see* figures | inside the app bundle | shipped (§6.7) |
| Auto-refresh hook | agents stay current | `~/.claude/settings.json` (managed entry) | **Connect** (Claude Code) (§8.8) |
| Live bridge | selection, live edits, `get_view` | per open project (`.meta/live/`) | automatic while a project is open |
| Project inbox | annotations + comments for agents | per project (`.meta/feedback.ndjson`, comment sidecars) | automatic |

The section references in this product table identify the Flux AI overhaul plan.
The bundle ships with Flux. **Connect** is the step that registers it with an agent.
See [Working with agents](collaboration.qmd) for annotations, routing and context.

## Troubleshooting

If a row is red, expand it and run **Fix** when offered. **Run doctor** gives the
latest execution evidence. **Use this Flux for agents** explicitly chooses this
installation when the launcher belongs to another checkout or install.

If a new skill does not appear, check its name and description in the frontmatter,
use **Re-publish**, and restart your agent session. Flux leaves edited and unmanaged
files alone; the row explains any collision or permission error.

If no sessions appear, run the copied connection command in the agent. Presence
appears after an explicit project connection and expires when its heartbeat stops.
The monitor does not start an agent or enable watch mode by itself.
